rationale: One pass over nums; each element uses average O(1) dictionary lookup and insert.
One pass over adjacent character pairs, with constant-time dictionary lookups per pair.
Each character is pushed or popped at most once, with constant work per character.
Binary search halves the [l, r) range on each iteration.
The loop runs n times with constant work per step; using the standard unit-cost arithmetic model.
Single pass; average O(1) dictionary lookups and inserts per element.
Each nums2 element is pushed once and popped at most once, so stack work is O(n); final list comprehension is O(m).
Checks fixed-position entries; membership tests an edge list of length two.
Each recursive call discards about half of k, giving O(log(m + n)) depth; two searches remain logarithmic. Assumes inf is imported from math.

There are k sliding-window passes over about m/k words each; each word slice/hash costs O(k), and each word enters/leaves the window at most once. Counter(words) also costs proportional to total input word characters. Empty words fails at words[0].

Backtracking tries up to 9 digits for each of E empty cells; pruning helps in practice. With a fixed 9x9 board this is technically bounded, but the standard algorithmic analysis is exponential. Unsolvable board may retain stale digits.
Linear passes build the left/right maxima and sum the result. Empty height raises IndexError.
Memoization bounds evaluation to at most (m+1)(n+1) states with constant work per state. Recursion depth can reach about m+n and exceed Python limits.

Grid and UnionFind initialization cost O(m*n); each of k positions checks up to four neighbors and performs near-constant amortized union-find work. The a-1 IDs are shifted but remain one-to-one with Python negative-index wrap for arrays of exactly m*n entries; fragile in ports or changed array sizes.
Cached DFS computes each matrix cell once with four neighbor checks. Recursion can reach m*n on a snake-like path and exceed Python limits; empty matrix raises IndexError at matrix[0].
Adjacency construction and each of two DFS traversals are O(n) for a tree. Recursion depth can reach n on a path-shaped tree and exceed Python limits; n=1 works.
Each character enters the set once and is removed at most once; pointers move forward and set operations are average O(1). Empty input returns 0.
Nested loops fill about n^2/2 table cells, each in O(1). Lower triangle and diagonal provide correct bases; empty input returns an empty string.

There are 13 fixed denominations and a bounded number of symbols for valid input. For values above 3999, repeated M output grows linearly in num/output length; nonpositive values return an empty string.

Each digit multiplies combinations by at most four; each resulting string is rebuilt by concatenation, costing O(n) per final-level string. Digits 0 and 1 are unsupported but valid input is 2-9; empty input returns [].
Each iteration halves the search interval and the final check is O(1). Assumes distinct values; empty input raises IndexError.
Performs two binary searches and constant-time result handling. Searching target+1 assumes integer values; empty array is handled.
Nested loops perform about n^2/2 recurrence updates and the DP array has n+1 entries. Python big-integer arithmetic adds cost for large n; n=0 returns 1.
Graph construction and Kahn topological traversal process each vertex and edge a constant number of times. Cycles yield an empty result; no recursion.
Each value is pushed once and popped at most once. inf must be imported from math.
At most every character of every string is compared, bounded by total input size; n is number of strings and m is the first string length. Empty strs raises IndexError.
One in-place pass. Assumes sorted input; empty list returns 0.
One in-place pass; input need not be sorted.
Binary search over [0, x]; mid is positive whenever division occurs, and x=0 returns 0.
Always checks 12*60 fixed time pairs with bounded bit-count work.
Counter processes input once; the follow-up pass is bounded by the alphabet size.
One frequency-count pass and one pass over distinct values; missing Counter entries read as zero.
One pass over E trust edges and one pass over n people; n=1 with no edges returns 1.
Cache bounds evaluation to at most (m+1)(n+1) states with constant work each; recursion depth may reach m+n and hit Python limits.
Single dynamic-programming pass with constant-time transitions; empty input returns 0.
Both window pointers move only forward, so shrinking is amortized linear. Empty t causes an index error; inf must be imported.
No memoization; explores many valid prefix splits and output can itself be exponential. Prefix slicing and trie lookup add polynomial overhead; recursion depth can reach n.
reviewed_complexity: Exponential, O(2^n) worst case plus polynomial overhead

rationale: When midpoint equals right value, right decreases by only one; duplicate-heavy/all-equal input degrades to linear. Empty input raises IndexError.
reviewed_complexity: O(log n) average, O(n) worst case

rationale: C is total characters and U distinct letters. Edge extraction is linear in C; matrix scan/topological work is O(U^2). Fixed alphabet size 26 makes matrix work constant. Assumes the omitted implementation handles prefixes and cycles as intended.
Up to O(N) splits; each subsequence selection is linear and suffix-comparison merges can cost O(k^2) each. Recursive suffix comparison depth can be O(k).
BFS visits each tree node once and processes each edge a constant number of times. Division occurs only when an unvisited neighbor exists.
Two pointers move inward at most n-1 times; fewer than two bars returns 0.
Sorting precedes an outer scan and two-pointer pass. The original packet advances both pointers and skips duplicates after a match.
reviewed_complexity: O(n^2) after sorting, plus O(n log n) sort

rationale: Split, scan, and join are linear in path length; root-level .. is ignored.
Each distinct value is removed from the set at most once; remaining lookups are expected O(1). defaultdict may add O(n) keys.
There are O(n^2) substring checks, and slicing plus hashing a substring costs proportional to its length; textbook O(n^2) assumes constant-time slices.
One stack pass. Operand pop order is correct and int(float division) truncates toward zero, but float division can lose precision for huge integers; empty tokens raises IndexError.
Both pointers move forward; each character is added and removed at most once.
Kahn topological traversal processes each vertex and edge a constant number of times; appending while iterating over the Python list queue is valid.
